compatibleChanges.rationale: Adds the optional developerDir field: a local client's DEVELOPER_DIR, overlaid on the env of commands the daemon spawns for that request. A released daemon ignores the unknown meta key and keeps its own environment, exactly as before; a released client never sends it, so the new daemon inherits its own environment for that request. The remote HTTP surface strips it. Also adds the optional leaseRetainOnClose field, sent only on lease_allocate when the caller opts in: a released daemon ignores the unknown meta key and releases the lease on session close as before, and a released client never sends it. Adds the optional providerCredentialFingerprint field: a digest of the local caller's provider credential variables, which the daemon compares with its own on lease_allocate. A released daemon ignores the unknown meta key and allocates as before; a released client never sends it, so the new daemon skips the comparison. The client sends it only to a local daemon, and the remote HTTP surface strips it.

#2747 adds the 'screen-recording-contact-sheet' literal for the PNG that `record contact-sheet` publishes beside the recording it read. DaemonArtifactType already widens to `(string & {})`, so an artifactType value outside the known set was always valid on the wire; the literal only sharpens the type hint for code that opts into recognizing it. A released peer that does not know it never requests that field in a download and parses the artifact record by its `field`, so it carries the sheet as an unknown artifact instead of failing.

#2246 adds the optional isDirectory field. It is pure client-local state — never serialized, never sent to the daemon — that tells the CLIENT'S OWN download logic to extract a tar body instead of writing it verbatim; the GET /artifacts/:id request and response framing are unchanged. Every existing call site (screenshot, recording) omits it and keeps writing a single file exactly as before. The signature also names the client request as DaemonWireRequest and the response as the kernel DaemonResponse instead of the daemon package aliases; only compile-time type names moved.

#2246 selects a file or directory destination once. Directory downloads stage and safely extract beside the destination, propagate timeout cancellation through both operations, and atomically rename the complete top-level entry; returning that local path is client-only state. The GET /artifacts/:id request and response framing, and every existing file artifact call site's behavior, are unchanged.

#2246 passes isDirectory only for the new test-artifacts type and uses the exact path the client materializer published. Existing screenshot and recording artifacts still report their requested file path; only the new directory response gains its suite-invocation segment. The signature also names the client request as DaemonWireRequest and the response as the kernel DaemonResponse instead of the daemon package aliases; only compile-time type names moved. The function now takes the client host as a parameter and resolves a relative local path against its working directory instead of the process's; the client binds the same directory, so nothing a peer parses moves.

Adds the optional providerCredentialFingerprint parameter to agent_device.lease.allocate, forwarded only when the request meta carries one, which the client sets only for a local daemon. A released protocol-2 daemon ignores unknown JSON-RPC parameters, and a request without a fingerprint keeps the previous payload byte-for-byte. The signature also names the client request as DaemonWireRequest and the response as the kernel DaemonResponse instead of the daemon package aliases; only compile-time type names moved. It now composes the envelope through buildDaemonRpcRequest in @agent-device/contracts/lease-scope, which takes the request id from its caller; the client supplies the id it supplied before (the request meta id, else a fresh one), so envelope construction preserves method, params and id. Separately, credential fingerprint lookup now trims the provider name on both client and daemon. A whitespace-spelled provider can therefore add a fingerprint that the released client omitted; this changes fingerprint presence, not the envelope or optional parameter contract.

#2110 read the optional providerApp lease-allocation parameter into the existing flags bag; #2494 reads the full provider-allocation flag set into that same bag through the shared readLeaseAllocateProviderFlags projection, so the reconstructed req.flags handed to prepareSession match what the line transport forwards for free. Released protocol-2 clients omit these and follow the unchanged allocation path; no existing field is required or reinterpreted. The optional retainOnClose boolean parameter is read into meta.leaseRetainOnClose; a released daemon ignores it and keeps releasing on session close. Reads the optional providerCredentialFingerprint lease-allocation parameter into request meta, so a local caller over HTTP gets the same credential check as over the socket. A daemon with an auth hook treats every HTTP caller as remote and strips it, as it does developerDir. Released protocol-2 clients omit it and follow the unchanged allocation path; no existing field is required or reinterpreted. Reads or forwards the optional devicePin allocation parameter. Released clients omit it; older daemons ignore it. Existing fields keep their meanings under ADR 0006. Validates the optional devicePin metadata through the shared parser before dispatch. Existing valid pins and requests that omit a pin keep their request projection. Malformed pin objects now fail clearly with the existing INVALID_ARGS envelope and invalid_device_pin reason instead of a later TypeError. This repairs validation of an unreleased optional field; routes, authentication, framing, and existing fields are unchanged under ADR 0006.

DaemonError is now declared as an alias of NormalizedError, whose members were already field-for-field identical (code, message, cause, hint, diagnosticId, logPath, logPathUnavailable, diagnosticsRecord, retriable, supportedOn, details). No wire byte changes; only the declaration text moved.

details.dispatched is a new OPTIONAL field inside details, which was already an open record: an older peer ignores the key and every existing field keeps its shape. It carries no | unknown for whether a failed interaction reached the device (the dispatch-disclosure golden table).

#1801 and #1862 client-side only: this reads optional daemon error metadata, most recently the structured `cause`. Parsing of every previously read field is unchanged, so a released daemon's error payload is accepted exactly as before.

Inlined `decodeURIComponent`+catch replaced by the shared `decodeUriSegment` (packages/daemon/src/server/http-request-target.ts), which is listed and byte-identical in behaviour: the same artifact ids decode, and an undecodable id still resolves to the empty id the route rejects.

Implementation-only daemon changes under ADR 0006: #3753 passes the runtime host environment into archiving; #4165 uses a bounded, abortable Node pipeline and validates the declared byte length, with idempotent reader release after completion or failed setup. The handler waits for file readiness before setting headers and starting the pipeline, so open errors use the existing JSON error response. Setup errors clear artifact-only headers first. Successful status codes, headers and artifact bytes retain their existing contracts. Failed or incomplete streaming reads close the HTTP transfer instead of hanging; released clients already treat an interrupted download as failure. Routes, authorization and error JSON shapes are unchanged, so no peer must parse a new payload or send a new field. Implementation-only follow-up to #4165 under ADR 0006: response close cancels artifact preparation and streaming through an internal AbortSignal. Shared builds continue for other downloads. The existing streamed failure helper now owns the same pre-header JSON error and post-header connection destruction. Successful status, headers, bytes, routes and authorization retain their existing contracts; disconnected clients receive no new payload. A response that has finished writing is not cancelled by its normal close event, so successful pipeline completion keeps its existing success semantics. Caller cancellation is normalized to the existing request_canceled error instead of forwarding caller-supplied reasons. Artifact expiry and download deadlines keep their existing reasons. The shared HTTP disconnect helper preserves typed cancellation on aborted requests and unfinished response closes. Directory preparation counts inventory and download callers together, so one disconnected download cannot abort an inventory caller's build; successful response fields and authorization stay unchanged.
#3753 threads the daemon runtime's host environment into the same archive spawn from the inventory route. The JSON body it writes and the error path are unchanged; no peer-visible field moves.

#1801 and #1862 lift optional metadata onto the normalized error, most recently a redacted structured `cause`. No previously emitted field changes shape or value, and peers that do not know the field ignore it.

#1862 client-side only: this rehydrates the new optional structured `cause` when present. Released daemons that omit it follow the unchanged path, and no request field or existing response field is narrowed.

#2198 slice B teaches the client to read the `upstream` link a proxy's /health already nests. The field is optional and additive: a daemon or proxy that does not send it parses exactly as before, and no request shape changes. readHealthPayload reads the same top-level fields through readHealthLink and additionally the nested `upstream` object when present; a payload without it yields the previous shape.

#2198 checks every link a command RPC crosses for protocol skew. #2650 caps a retry health probe at the request's remaining deadline. Health payload parsing and protocol mismatch refusal are unchanged; released peers still receive the same RPCs. #3178 threads the caller's optional AbortSignal through so a canceled call cuts a probe already in flight instead of waiting it out: the signal is client-local, never serialized, and the GET /health request and payload are unchanged.

#2198 context: adds one optional field to the value this DAEMON-INTERNAL gate hands its own route handlers — sessionNamespace, the caller's tenant plus whether the daemon partitioned that caller's session names. Nothing about it is serialized: no request header is read that was not read before, no response field is added, and a refusal keeps the same 401 {ok:false,error,code} REST body sendRestJsonError already sent. What it enables is a refusal DROPPED, never one added — an unattested (client-declared) tenant no longer has the <tenant>: prefix rule applied to it, because scopeRequestSession never applied that prefix to its sessions either. A released peer that now gets 200 where it got 401 is getting the ndjson record it asked for and already parses.

#2198 context: widens the authorizer callback's result by the same optional sessionNamespace field, so the route can put its tenant question to session-tenant-scope instead of re-deriving the rule locally. The callback is supplied by createDaemonHttpServer inside this process and never crosses the wire; a caller of the route sends and parses exactly the bytes it did before.

#2198 context: asks isTenantAddressableSessionName instead of applying the prefix rule locally. Same UNAUTHORIZED code, same 'Session is outside this tenant' message and same 401 body for the attested-tenant case the rule still refuses; the only difference a peer can observe is that an unattested tenant now gets the 200 + ndjson record it already knows how to read instead of a 401 it could not act on. Implementation-only HTTP error repair under ADR 0006: setup failures use the shared streamed failure helper. Before headers, it emits the existing REST JSON error shape with an error status; after headers, it destroys the incomplete transfer. Successful diagnostics remain 200 with the same NDJSON bytes. Released clients reject error statuses before reading diagnostic records, so no successful response parser or request requirement changes.

#2266 adds the additive harmonyos-instance lease backend literal and #3229 the macos-app literal. Protocol-2 peers ignore a new backend unless it is explicitly requested, and an older daemon refuses macos-app with its existing unsupported-backend error; existing iOS/Android/HarmonyOS values and payloads remain unchanged.

#2266 derives the optional runtime platform from one shared vocabulary, adding harmonyos without changing existing iOS/Android payloads. Older peers can refuse the new value with the existing validation error.
#2266 broadens runtime-hint validation to accept the additive HarmonyOS platform value; existing protocol-2 runtime hints remain valid and unchanged.

#2894 lets an iOS runner start outlive the caller whose deadline gave up on it, so a progress event can arrive after the response ended. The sink now also skips a response whose writable side has ended, next to the destroyed check it already had. No byte written to a live response changes: the envelope framing and payload are untouched, and a released client never sees an event it could not have received before.

#4441 replaces the one 5-minute timer over a whole upload with the preparation aggregate that bounds it, and hands that aggregate's signal to the attempt. The request a peer parses is unchanged: same route, method, the headers buildUploadRequestHeaders produces, the piped payload and the 200/308 handling. What moved is when this client stops sending, and the ceiling is now shorter rather than longer, so a protocol-2 daemon or proxy answers the same requests and simply sees a stalled leg torn down sooner.

#4441 ends the direct-upload sequence when a transfer phase's own budget expires, instead of re-preflighting for a fresh ticket or falling back, because a second attempt would be permission that budget already refused. Preflight, ticket PUT and finalize requests are unchanged in route, method, headers and body, so a protocol-2 daemon parses everything it parsed before; it just receives no further legs once the caller's aggregate has expired.

#4441 drops the hint that named the removed 5-minute timeout, and an expired transfer phase is no longer treated as a transport break, so this route is not re-entered by a fallback after the client's own budget ended the attempt. The POST /upload request itself is unchanged: same method, headers, chunked body and response parsing. A protocol-2 daemon sees the identical request in every case that completes, and no further request in a stalled one.

The bounded body is local diagnostic context, not a new peer payload. Once the diagnostic prefix is full, further chunks are consumed without concatenating or copying that retained prefix; error status and diagnostic contents are unchanged. Released daemons already return 200 for successful artifact downloads, so supported skewed peers parse the same successful framing (ADR 0006).

The mapper now takes the normalized error (code plus details) instead of the code alone. A gone resource now answers 404 instead of 500: COMMAND_FAILED with details.reason RESOURCE_EXPIRED (an artifact, upload ticket, uploaded artifact or materialized path id the TTL registry no longer holds) maps to 404. The mapper also takes over the DEVICE_IN_USE human_control_active 423 rule, which statusCodeForDaemonError applied only to a failed response a /rpc handler returned. The rule now also reaches the REST routes and thrown /rpc failures, which answered 500: a PUT /admin/leases/<id> refused during a human-control hold, or a non-streamed /rpc call whose handler throws human_control_active, now answers 423. /admin/* is host-only on the loopback port and the proxy never forwards it, and the host already reads 423 for the same refusal on a returned /rpc failure. No released client branches on 404 versus 500 for these routes: downloadRemoteArtifactFromUrl treats any status >= 400 alike, the upload client fails any non-2xx and decides retries from a typed stream detail rather than the status, the /rpc client parses the JSON-RPC error envelope whatever the status and only special-cases 409, and the proxy passes the status through. The error code, message and JSON-RPC error data a peer parses are unchanged, so a protocol 2 peer reports the same failure it did before.

#4441 runs each attempt under a sequential phase watchdog (connect, body inactivity, response headers) and fails with the expired phase's own typed evidence instead of a transport error, and reads the response through a reader that reports bytes rather than the shared host-kit one. Bytes on the wire are unchanged: same route, method, headers, body framing, resume-offset handling and redirect limit. The client, not the response, chooses the local download path: a destination it registered in this request wins, a response localPath is accepted only on a record or trace stop or a perf stop or report, and any other artifact lands in cwd under the basename of its fileName. A released daemon echoes localPath equal to the registered destination for screenshot and test, and echoes an earlier destination only on those stop and report actions, so its artifacts land where they did before. The wire shape is unchanged.

The /rpc body limit is now DAEMON_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES (64 MiB), the one request limit the socket transport, the proxy default, and client writers share, raised from 1 MiB. A larger limit refuses nothing a released client sends; a new client refuses a request over 64 MiB before sending it, and a released daemon still answers anything between 1 MiB and 64 MiB with its own -32700 refusal, as before.

#4441 renames the constant naming this call's ceiling from UPLOAD_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS to UPLOAD_CONTROL_PLANE_TIMEOUT_MS because it governs finalize as well. The value is the same 30 seconds the released client used, and the request body, headers, route and redirect refusal are byte-for-byte unchanged, so a released daemon or proxy parses the identical request.

#4434 moves the actual Node Host/socket base-origin constructor from upload-http into shared ingress validation. It now requires one valid Host authority and derives the scheme from the socket instead of forwarding headers. The adopted publicOrigin migration changes deployment authority configuration, not the upload ticket URL string, authentication headers, body fields, 308 range framing, or finalize format that protocol-2 clients parse. Clients send the returned absolute URL as before. Configured origins are selected separately by the daemon constructor; no existing payload field is removed or reinterpreted.

#4434 accepts optional query components on the existing POST upload, preflight and finalize routes. Existing query-free paths and methods resolve identically; direct-upload IDs still exclude the query. This broadens accepted request targets without removing a route or changing any response framing under ADR 0006.

#4434 passes the origin validated by the HTTP ingress owner, or the explicitly configured publicOrigin, into the existing ticket producer. Protocol-2 clients receive the same uploadId and upload URL/header object, use the returned absolute URL, and keep the existing byte, range, authentication and finalize contracts. Forwarding headers no longer select authority under the documented operator migration; no wire field becomes required or changes interpretation.
